answer: One defense is pricing admission with bonded, peer-attested work history instead of self-declared identity. Peers deal only with keys whose jobs were countersigned. A sybil mints thousands of free keys, but each starts with no sable trail of completed work, so it must do real tasks first. Newcomers may join a lotus-style quorum instead: unrelated agents vouch jointly and post collateral slashed if the newcomer cheats. Faking an identity needs colluding signers and locked value at risk. The lantern is the public ledger, where shared guarantors behind a thousand clones illuminate one cluster.
